en.title: Integers Without Repeated Digits in a Range
en.description:
Given the closed interval [a,b], count the integers whose decimal representation has no repeated digit. The number 0 also counts as a valid integer.

The original rules are clear; this site adds the handling of zero, the upper bound and the standard input/output.

Source: https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/agoda#4-unique-digits-in-range (fixed statement fingerprint ad4afecb26c3a62396e8e4b999faf5b687be79b6f45cc5a926065788b53659ce). The input/output protocol and bounds added by this site follow the statement and are not claimed to be rules of the original site.
en.input: One line with two integers a b (0≤a≤b≤10^18).
en.output: Output the number of integers in the interval whose decimal digits are all distinct.
en.explanation: See the companion notes for the full approach, proof and complexity.
hints: First count the positive integers with fewer digits, then go digit by digit and enumerate valid choices smaller than the current bound digit; count the remaining positions by the number of permutations of the unused digits. Finally take the difference of the prefix function to get the interval answer.
